hypotheses.claim: JPA/Hibernate materializes a full entity for each result row, incurring ~0.02 ms per row.
hypotheses.mechanism: CustomerPaymentRepository.findRecent executes a JPQL query; Hibernate creates a RecentPaymentDto for each row, copying column values into a new object.
evidence: p50 latency grows from 4.2 ms (1 row) to 9.3 ms (100 rows) while server‑side SQL stays at ~0.2‑0.4 ms
response body size grows linearly 122 bytes per row
hypotheses.prediction: Changing the repository to a projection query (SELECT new RecentPaymentDto(...)) will reduce latency by ~2 ms for 100 rows.

hypotheses.claim: Jackson serializes each DTO to JSON, costing ~0.04 ms per row (≈0.0004 ms per byte).
hypotheses.mechanism: RecentPaymentsController returns a List<RecentPaymentDto>; Spring MVC uses Jackson to write the list as JSON, iterating over every field of every DTO.
evidence: body bytes per row = 122 B; latency increase ≈5.1 ms when moving from 1 to 100 rows → 5.1 ms / (122 B·99) ≈0.00042 ms per byte
SQL time is negligible, so the remaining per‑row growth must be CPU work after the query
hypotheses.prediction: Enabling Jackson Afterburner or switching to a streaming JSON writer will cut the latency gain for 100 rows by ~3 ms.

hypotheses.claim: Fixed Spring MVC / service dispatch overhead accounts for ~0.5 ms per request.
hypotheses.mechanism: Controller method entry, service call, repository call, and response handling introduce fixed Java‑method‑call and Spring MVC processing costs.
evidence: Even with a single row the non‑SQL part of latency is ~4.0 ms (4.2 ms total – 0.2 ms SQL). After subtracting estimated per‑row costs (≈2 ms ORM + ≈1 ms serialization for 1 row) ≈0.5 ms remains.
Latency does not drop below ~4 ms when rows are removed, indicating a constant base cost.
hypotheses.prediction: A minimal endpoint that returns an empty JSON array will still take ~0.5 ms.

probes_run.result: p50 latency 4.2 ms, 1 row, 122 B body, SQL 0.2 ms. Shows constant base cost + per‑row cost.
p50 latency 9.3 ms, 100 rows, 12 317 B body, SQL 0.4 ms. Linear growth with rows and bytes isolates per‑row cost.
